P0400.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0400 is the general flow fault of EGR system A, used where the module does not classify the error as too little (P0401) or too much (P0402).
s: Pinging under load or rough idle, depending on direction
c: EGR passages or valve carboned up
Leak in the intake or EGR pipe

P0401.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0401 means too little exhaust is recirculated.
c: EGR passages, valve or cooler carboned up
EGR valve faulty or stuck closed
Ford: DPFE sensor or its hoses blocked, cracked or swapped
Diesel: air mass meter drifting or air leak after the turbo
Vacuum control of the valve faulty

P0402.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0402 means too much exhaust is recirculated, or exhaust flows although the valve should be closed – CARB explicitly requires a leaking valve to be detected.
s: Diesel: black smoke, loss of power
c: EGR valve stuck open, dirt under the seat
Ford: DPFE sensor drifting or hose wrong
Diesel: air leak between air mass meter and turbo, MAF drift

P0403.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0403 concerns the electrical drive of the EGR valve – solenoid, stepper motor, DC motor or vacuum regulator.
s: EGR switched off: pinging (petrol) or higher NOx
c: Connector at the EGR valve corroded or loose
Coil or motor in the EGR valve burnt out

P0404.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. P0404 is the function check of the valve drive: on valves with a position sensor the module compares commanded and actual position, and a persistent deviation means the valve sticks, is coked or its drive is too weak (GM diesel 2018 above 10 %, GM petrol 2004 above 15 %, both MIL after two trips).
s: Rough idle or jerking if the valve hangs open
c: Position sensor in the valve inaccurate
Supply voltage too low or ground fault

P0405.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR sensor A is usually the valve position sensor with a 5 V supply; on Ford until about 2011 it was the DPFE differential pressure sensor.
c: Wire or connector to the EGR valve open or shorted to ground
Position sensor in the EGR valve faulty (usually one unit with the valve)

P0406.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. EGR sensor A is usually the valve position sensor; on Ford until about 2011 the DPFE differential pressure sensor.

Signal wire shorted to 5 V or positive
Sensor in the EGR valve faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

P0407.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor B is depends on the manufacturer – on systems with a second valve or pressure sensor it is that second sensor.
s: EGR or EGR cooler protection possibly restricted

P0408.d: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) routes part of the exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and NOx. What EGR sensor B is depends on the manufacturer – on systems with a second valve or pressure sensor it is that second sensor.

EGR valve with integrated sensor faulty

s: Substitute value used, EGR cooler check suspended
c: Connector or wire at the sensor (heat, corrosion)

c: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafed on the exhaust)

Ground wire open or short to positive

s: Check engine light on, may come and go
c: Loose contact in the connector or chafed wire
Sensor with an internal hairline crack

P040F.d: The two EGR temperature sensors measure the gas temperature in the EGR path, before and after the cooler – which is A and which is B depends on the maker. P040F compares sensors A and B: after a long stop (GM: at least 8 hours) both must read about ambient temperature.
s: Check engine light on, may come and go
c: Contact resistance at one sensor's connector

P0410.d: After a cold start the secondary air (AIR) pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; a shut-off valve opens the path and stops exhaust from flowing back. P0410 is the general function code for secondary air system A.

Pump silent after a cold start, or unusually loud
c: Secondary air pump failed (water ingress, seized)
Combination or shut-off valve carboned up or stuck
Vacuum hose or electric changeover valve leaking or faulty
Air ducts in the head carboned up or hose off

P0411.d: After a cold start the secondary air (AIR) pump blows fresh air behind the exhaust valves so that unburnt fuel burns off and the catalyst heats up faster; a shut-off valve opens the path and stops exhaust from flowing back. P0411 means the measured air flow does not match the expected value.
s: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
Pump silent after a cold start, or unusually loud
c: Pump weak or failed (water, filter debris)
Combination valve partly stuck or check valve faulty
Hoses blocked, leaking or off; ducts in the head carboned up
Pressure sensor port blocked or sensor drifting (pressure-sensor systems)
Pump relay or supply with contact resistance

P0412.d: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0412 is the general electrical fault in the control circuit of valve A, detected by comparing the driver's feedback with its commanded state.
s: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
c: Switching valve A faulty (coil open or shorted, water ingress)
Connector corroded or wire open or chafed

P0413.d: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. P0413 means the control circuit of valve A is open: with the driver switched off the module does not see the expected supply or pull-up level.
s: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)
c: Wire to the valve open or connector loose or corroded
Fuse of the valve supply blown

P0414.d: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. s: Secondary air readiness not set (emission test)

Wire chafed against ground or supply
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

P0415.d: The switching valve is the electrically driven valve of this path – a solenoid valve, or on Pierburg/VW systems an electric changeover valve that applies vacuum to the pneumatic combination valve; valve A serves the first path or bank 1, valve B the second. s: Radiator fan does not run, or runs constantly
Overheating at standstill or in traffic
c: Fan relay (coil open) or fan control module faulty
Connector at fan or relay corroded, water ingress or pin pushed out
Control wire open or shorted to ground
Fan motor or fan assembly faulty

Control wire open or shorted to ground

P0482.d: The engine module switches cooling fan stages through relays, pulling each relay coil to ground. P0482 concerns the control circuit of the third stage or relay: with the driver off the line should sit at battery voltage through the coil, and the internal pull-up level means an open circuit (Saab ME9: more than 1 s, 10–18 V, engine running).
s: One fan stage fails – temperature rises in traffic or when towing
c: Fan relay 3 faulty (coil open) or not seated properly
Control wire open or high-resistance, corroded or backed-out pins
Relay coil supply missing (fuse, supply wire)

P0483.d: Two kinds of cooling fan carry these codes: electric fans switched by relays or driven by a PWM/LIN fan module with speed feedback, and engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch, whose speed a Hall sensor reports – GM calls them EV fans, meaning electro-viscous, not electric vehicle. P0483 checks the fan's function, not its circuit.

Constant fan roar, or temperature rise at standstill

Radiator or condenser clogged, coolant low (Subaru logic)

P0484.d: P0484 monitors the current drawn in the fan's load circuit: if it exceeds a threshold – blocked or stiff motor, shorted turns, a short in the load circuit – the code sets. s: Fan does not run, runs only briefly or at reduced power
Humming or grinding at the fan, possibly blown fan fuse

Shorted turns or worn brushes in the fan motor
Short in the load circuit (pinched or chafed wire)
Fan control module faulty (wrong current measurement)

P0485.d: P0485 monitors the supply or ground path of the fan or its control module – not the control line. It is typical of fans with their own module (PWM or LIN), which can report undervoltage or a missing ground.

c: Fan or fan module ground loose, corroded or broken
Fan fuse blown or fuse holder overheated or corroded
Relay power contact burnt – voltage drop under load
Connector at the fan scorched, water ingress
